title: Sports and Recreation
goal: Join or decline a game, ask about a lesson or facility, and use clear language during a team activity.

runs.text: Choose the sports relevant to you. These brief meanings identify activities; they do not teach their rules.

rows.text: A bat-and-ball team game involving running around bases.
A team game aiming to score in the other team's basket.
A team game carrying, throwing and kicking a ball toward scoring areas.
A team game aiming to kick the ball into a goal.
Racket sports using a ball / a shuttlecock.
Moving through water by using your body.
A team game on ice using skates, sticks and a puck.
A combat sport using gloved fists.
A game using clubs to hit a ball into holes.
A bat-and-ball team game using small sets of upright posts called wickets.
A team game using an oval ball that players carry, pass and kick.

Fictional recreation-center information: beginner tennis lessons Saturday at 10 a.m.; experienced-player lessons at 11; swimming sessions from 3 to 5 p.m., booked at the desk; basketball practice Tuesday at 6 p.m. on Court 4. The badminton court is Court 2, past the desk and through the first door on the left.

blocks.caption: Communicate during a game · Casey & Jordan

runs.text: sends the ball to a teammate;
attempts to score. Short calls can fit a fast-moving game.
alerts a teammate to an opponent in the stated scene.
asks which side has possession or the next play. The exact meaning depends on the sport and moment.
A friend invites you to the Tuesday basketball practice. Ask where and when, then accept or decline. Your partner uses the center information.
You want beginner tennis. Ask about the group and how to sign up. Then ask about the unknown cost instead of inventing a price.
Ask where the badminton court is. The employee gives the supplied directions. Repeat them to check:
Past the desk, first door on the left?
In the basketball scene, call for a pass and report a missed shot. Change the next cue: you did not hear your teammate. Say
Choose three sports you want to talk about. Cover their meanings and describe one. Then say whether you want to play, watch or learn it.

“Which court, and what time? — Court four at six. — Count me in.” / “I'd like the beginner tennis lesson. What does it cost?” / “So Court Two is past the desk, through the first door on the left?” / “I missed it. Let's try again.” / “I'd like to learn tennis.”
say both roles without performing a physical game. On a later round, change your availability or the sport.

Did you communicate your intention, confirm the activity's details, and make calls the teammate could understand? Did you keep an unanswered price or booking question separate from a confirmed arrangement?
